\begin{figure}[!tbp]
  \centering
  \includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{../figures/out/rse_fig_area.pdf}
  \caption{\textbf{Agreement in flooded area is not agreement in shoreline position.}
  (a)~Area bias of each grid's predicted sea in the study domain, (predicted $-$ observed) as a percentage of the observed sea, at every level of the rising limb (E1), early fall (E2) and late fall (E3) (\metric{rev.s.item4.area_bias.shape.gebco2026.domain.n_units} units per grid), after each grid's area-fitted vertical offset.
  Open triangles: values beyond the axis, listed in the panel.
  (b)~Out-of-sample test of the offset: late-fall area bias in the calibration and test blocks, with the offset fitted on all periods' training blocks (open) or on E1 and E2 only (filled).
  Markers: the median over the $n = \metric{rev.s.item4.oos.gebco2026.calibtest.c_e12.n_units}$ late-fall levels; bars: \metric{params.iqr_lo_pct}th to \metric{params.iqr_hi_pct}th percentile.
  (c)~Three ways of fitting a grid's vertical datum to flooded area on the training blocks: one offset for the domain (the main analysis), one per sector, and a planar offset field (linear in easting and northing).
  Left: the summed absolute area error over training-block units, which each fit minimises.
  Right: the median over the seven sectors of each sector's median shoreline displacement.
  The planar field was audited for GEBCO\_2026 and ETOPO1 only.}
  \label{fig:rse_area}
\end{figure}
